releaseNotes: Made the prepared specialist roster executable end to end. Every role now resolves parent contracts, repository context packs, conditional nested skills, current tool routes, outputs, and verification into a fresh-context node brief with a mandatory knowledge receipt. Generated repos bootstrap APP_AGENTS.md and all role prompts before the first worker. Added a real Codex/Claude/Cursor headless executor, strict output and receipt checks, and standing authority with persisted envelope/action provenance plus dispatch-time revalidation of exact target, payload, capability, spend, and voice scope. Operator readiness is now a graph dependency before parallel app and landing work, verifies all launch capabilities up front, and records both protected control waivers and exact workflow-scoped envelopes for deployment, assets, store surfaces, and test uploads. Registered every prepared role in the catalog, routed each through live workflows, allowed narrowly approved provider/public/test-upload work with before/readback proof, and added structural and behavioral regressions for prompt nesting, roster coverage, design fan-out, and approval matching.

Added operator-ready step-away onboarding before build work. The opening exchange now resolves autonomy, budget, required accounts, durable operator roles, deployment targets, signing and store-upload access, asset tools, and optional final-release scope together. Added a prepared operator-readiness prompt, explicit website/asset/App Store/Play capability starters, standing envelopes for deploys, asset work, store metadata/media, and test-build uploads, automatic reuse without repeat prompts, consolidated missing-access handoffs, validator-backed ledger policies, and LaunchBench regressions for late preflight and approval re-prompts.

Made design acceptance start a parallel app-and-landing fan-out. Split local landing creation from founder-gated publication, added a launch-surface producer prompt with initial-build, impact-audit, and bounded-update modes, and required continuous synchronization across landing onboarding, copy, approved prices, screenshots, marketing assets, Apple product pages, and Google Play listings. Added a design_contract_lock cascade, Google Play surface edges, graph fixtures, and a LaunchBench regression scenario.

Made design/design.md the single design contract and connected it to Design Room state, tokens, rendering, product, onboarding, landing, store, growth, lifecycle, and implementation checks. Moved Design Room seed state to studio/seed, fixed stale-render defaults, retained legacy import compatibility, and added semantic parity fixtures. Added bounded expert prompts for research, product, design, copy, marketing, mobile, backend, security, accessibility/device QA, and customer success, with disjoint scopes and a fixed handoff. Added enforced delegation reasons, concise founder updates, aggregate service readiness, contradiction and stale-copy checks, evidence-aware proof results, and a Git source-checkpoint gate.

Added the UGC Realism Prompt Structure to tool-recipes/visual-and-motion-production.md: a realism-first prompt register for believable-person UGC (Seedance 2.5), sitting beside the premium Product Ad Structure and explicitly scoped as its opposite -- the UGC-family Marketing Studio modes now route to realism principles (social context truth, imperfect presence, thought-while-talking, alive environment, no resolution), a literal first-frame prompt template (GPT Image 2 realism-keyword stack), and a literal second-by-second Seedance video prompt template, while tv_spot keeps the four-beat premium structure. Added Recipe 7 (Script-First Believable-Person UGC): first frame to Seedance 2.5 reference video with no Soul or avatar required, gated on a judge-panel-surviving script, with a converted-reference shortcut (1:1 timestamped breakdown of an already-converting UGC video via video_analysis_create or Gemini), a raw-footage edit pass, a human believability test, and the existing virality/founder gates. ugc-creator-engine.md gains the Script Bank And Judge Panel discipline: per-lens fresh-context judges (pacing, vocabulary, idea strength, structure) with at least one grounded in a real creator's transcript corpus, 10+ scripts per batch, and a hard no-generation-before-panel-verdict gate for synthetic UGC; the synthetic-UGC guardrails now state the prompt-register split, the believability test, automation-last, and scope the Soul/avatar requirement to founder-face content only (Recipe 7 needs neither). Seedance 2.0 mentions in visual-and-motion-production.md model intent, onboarding-conversion.md, and app-store-listing-prep.md updated to Seedance 2.5 with confirm-model-id language, since 2.5 is the first version whose skin texture passes as human. Source material: the founder-supplied Seedance 2.5 master UGC system prompt and AI-UGC workflow guide, adapted into this skill's recipe/gate structure with external pricing and platform URLs left out as volatile (live pricing is verified at the paid-tool-routing spend confirmation instead). PR review (Codex) caught four real gaps, all fixed. First and largest: the script-gate and believability rules lived only in knowledge prose, so an engine run could spend on and approve synthetic UGC with every audit green -- the exact enforcement-words-not-work trap this repo already documented. check-content-assets.ts now detects UGC-family manifest assets (mode/route/render_proof matching ugc, ugc_how_to, ugc_unboxing, product_review; asset_id excluded on purpose so a name is not a mode claim) and errors on missing script_id or judge_verdict, and at done-tier statuses on a pending judge_verdict or a missing/pending believability result. Three fail-then-catch fixtures prove the gate fires on a scriptless UGC asset and an approved-without-believability asset, and stays quiet on a compliant one; the workspace manifest template and CONTENT_ASSETS.md field list gained the three fields with teaching placeholders. Second: Recipe 7's recorded-field list omitted prompt_brief even though check-content-assets rejects Higgsfield-routed assets without a design-token brief, so the documented happy path failed the validator -- prompt_brief is now carried in step 5 and step 9, with the split stated (design tokens govern app UI in frame, the realism register governs person and scene). Third: the converted-reference shortcut skipped the first-frame step while the video step still required a first-frame reference, leaving the shortcut path with no reference image -- the shortcut now replaces only the video-prompt skeleton and the first-frame step always runs. Fourth: the new prose used long compound sentences and metaphor against the repo's ASD-STE100 policy for knowledge/*.md -- the added sections in both files were rewritten into short, literal sentences (the fenced prompt templates are payload, not documentation, and keep their register). A second Codex round caught four more real gaps in the new gate itself, all fixed. First: detection relied on provider text (route/mode/render_proof), so a Recipe 7 asset routed as bare seedance_2_5 dodged every gate -- every generated-video asset (Seedance/Marketing Studio/Cinema Studio/Veo routes) must now declare asset_kind from a fixed vocabulary, and asset_kind: ugc activates the gates; silence is no longer a classification. Second: script_id accepted any nonempty string while no script bank existed anywhere -- script_id must now parse as <bank path>#<format-id>, the bank file must exist, and the format id must be recorded in it; a durable ugc/script-bank.md template with the judge-verdict columns ships in the workspace. Third: the verdict check rejected only 'pending', so 'rejected by the panel' passed at approved -- a failed/rejected judge_verdict now errors at any status, and done-tier statuses require passed/survived wording. Fourth: believability treated any nonempty non-pending value as success, so 'viewer identified it as AI' passed at approved -- done-tier statuses now require an explicit passed result and reject failed. Fixture coverage grew from three to seven cases: the Seedance dodge, the unrecorded script anchor, the failing verdict, and the failed believability are each proven caught, and the positive control moved to approved status with a resolving script, passing verdict, passing believability, and on-disk output so every done-tier branch is exercised on the pass path too. A third Codex round caught two more real gaps in the hardened gate, both fixed. First: anchor resolution was a substring search over any named file, so the positive path accepted a pointer to the template's own placeholder row, and a format id planted in any workspace file counted as a bank -- script_id must now name a script-bank.md file, the id must equal a table row's Format ID cell, and at a done-tier status that row must hold non-placeholder hook/script text and a row verdict whose prefix is passed/survived, reconciling the bank with the manifest claim. Second: the pass checks searched for the word 'passed' anywhere, so 'not passed -- panel did not approve' satisfied both the judge and believability gates -- both now parse the documented verdict prefix instead of searching free text. Four more fail-then-catch fixtures (wrong-bank pointer, placeholder row at approved, negated judge verdict, negated believability) plus a shared surviving-row builder keep the seven earlier cases green, for eleven total. A fourth Codex round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: every script/verdict check was tiered on done statuses, so a draft asset whose output file already existed -- generation spend already consumed -- was indistinguishable from a planned template entry, and the documented no-generation-before-panel gate was unenforceable at exactly the moment it matters. An on-disk output now activates the script gate at any status: the manifest verdict and the referenced bank row must both pass once generation evidence exists, while the shipped template (whose out/ directory does not exist) keeps teaching with pending placeholders. Believability stays done-tier, since the human test legitimately happens after generation. Second: script-bank paths were joined onto the workspace root without containment, so ../ traversal or a symlinked bank could satisfy the durable-script gate with another checkout's passing row -- the path is now resolved lexically and through realpath, and anything outside the audited root errors as bank_outside_workspace. Three more fail-then-catch fixtures (traversal bank, symlink-escape bank, spent draft with pending verdict) bring the UGC gate suite to fourteen cases. A fifth Codex round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: Recipe 7 generated the paid first frame in step 3 but obtained the founder's protected spend approval in step 4 -- the steps are swapped, and the approved ceiling now explicitly covers both image and video credits. Second: generation evidence was only an output file on disk, but a provider-backed generation spends credits before any file is downloaded -- a nonempty source_job_id or a remote output URL now also activates the script gate, with two more fail-then-catch fixtures (provider job id, remote URL) bringing the suite to sixteen cases. The shipped template stays a planned entry: its source_job_id is empty and its outputs are local paths that do not exist yet. A sixth Codex round caught one more real gap: the prompt_brief requirement was keyed on the route containing higgsfield or marketing_studio, so the bare seedance_2_5 route Recipe 7 permits could omit the design/DESIGN.md brief entirely -- the requirement now keys on the same generated-video detection the asset_kind rule uses, with a bare-Seedance-route fixture proving the catch (seventeen UGC gate cases total).

Fixed installed-runtime audits so Formation's repository-front-door no-slop gate runs only in a source checkout, while installed skill packages continue to exercise its synthetic positive and negative LaunchBench controls instead of resolving an unrelated parent Codex directory as the repository root. Runtime synchronization now installs dependencies with npm ci so npm-version-specific optional-platform metadata cannot rewrite the mirrored lockfile and break byte-parity certification.

Added knowledge/engineering/technical-documentation-ste100.md: this repo's technical documentation (architecture docs, engineering specs, ADRs, runbooks, API/config references, this skill's own knowledge/*.md files) now follows Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) -- flat, literal, one-meaning-per-word -- instead of no-slop-writing.md's voice-preserving rules. Wired via a new domain.engineering catalog reference (reference.engineering.technical-documentation-ste100) so the loadWhen graph pulls it in automatically. Placement resolved via llm-council: excludes root README.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which stay with no-slop-writing.md's existing check:no-slop gate, and defers engine-generated business-repo docs to a later, separately scoped change. Cross-linked from no-slop-writing.md section 8. Reference-only for now; a mechanical gate extension is a logged follow-up, not built in this change.
Added a one-line 'Documentation style' pointer to root AGENTS.md so the repo-wide policy has a home before any catalog-graph discovery happens.

PR review (Codex) caught two real gaps, both fixed. First: the reference's trigger line named engineering/TECH_SPEC.md, engineering/ENGINEERING_PLAN.md, and engineering/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md as governed files, but every file with those three names in this repository is actually a workspace/business/engineering/ or workspace-template/ generated-business template -- the exact surface the same file's §2 excludes. Reworded the trigger and §2 to name a maintainer-authored spec instead, with the exclusion stated by path. Second, and larger: the standard was reference-only, so catalog/audit checks passed even if a governed document violated every rule -- 'always uses ASD-STE100' was not enforceable. Resolved via llm-council (First Principles' framing won 3/3 in anonymous peer review): built check:documentation-ste100 (validation/business/engineering/check-technical-docs-ste100.ts), a mechanical two-rule subset -- sentence length and a present-perfect heuristic -- at two severity tiers mirroring check-no-slop.ts's own front-door split. Error tier applies today to the one file this change can guarantee compliant (the reference itself, which the new checker caught failing its own 20-word rule 13 times on first run -- real signal, not a rubber stamp -- and was rewritten into short sentences and bullet lists until it passed clean). Warning tier applies repo-wide to the rest of the governed knowledge/**/*.md surface (excluding knowledge/words/, which keeps no-slop-writing.md's register), giving real, non-blocking signal on pre-existing prose. Five fail-then-catch fixture cases in repo-gates.fixtures.ts prove the checker fires on both rules and respects the tier split, not just that it passes. Two peer-review-caught parser bugs fixed live: markdown bullet items were merging into one oversized sentence (list items now force their own boundary), and a colon-introduced clause or list now also ends a sentence chunk.

A second Codex review round on the same file caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: the reference's own trigger line names this skill's own README.md and SKILL.md as governed, but the checker's file discovery never enqueued either one -- an edit to either received no signal at all. Added both, relative to --skill-root so the fix stays root-agnostic. Second: a trailing prose paragraph with no terminal punctuation (no `.`/`!`/`?`/`:` before end of file) fell off the end of the sentence-matching regex entirely, so an oversized or present-perfect closing sentence passed silently as long as the file just stopped instead of ending in punctuation. Fixed by forcing a boundary at the end of the joined text when one is not already present. Two new fail-then-catch fixtures prove both fixes: one confirms README.md now gets scanned, one confirms a violation in an unterminated final sentence is still caught.

A third Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: docs/platform/technical-architecture.md and docs/platform/product-architecture.md -- current, real architecture docs -- were outside the checker's hardcoded docs/ list, so an edit to either got no signal despite the repo policy governing architecture docs. Added both paths explicitly (a full dynamic docs/ scan was considered and rejected: docs/brainstorms/, docs/plans/, and point-in-time historical audits under docs/platform/ are deliberately exploratory or frozen-record prose this repo's own conventions already keep outside every gate, so a blanket scan would pull in files that were never meant to be governed). Second, and more serious: the prior round's 'colon also ends a chunk' fix (added to stop a bullet-list intro from merging into its first item) was a real regression -- it let a single long grammatical sentence with a mid-sentence colon (`Follow this procedure: open the file, ...`) escape the 20-word ceiling by splitting into two short-looking halves that each passed individually. Replaced the blanket colon rule with a narrow, structural one: a line ending in ':' converts to a real boundary only when the very next line is a list item, so a list-introducing colon still gets its boundary while an ordinary colon-joined sentence stays one sentence for counting purposes. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this: a mid-sentence-colon instruction over the ceiling is caught, the same construction under the ceiling still passes, and the narrow exception is proven narrow (no false boundary when no list follows).

A fourth Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed -- the second time in a row a hardcoded path list missed a currently-existing governed file, so the discovery mechanism itself was the real problem, not the missing entry. First: validation/repository/source-freshness-maintenance.md, an active maintenance runbook the reference's own scope names ('a runbook'), was outside every discovery path (not under docs/ or knowledge/). Replaced the ad hoc per-round path patching with an explicit, extensible ADDITIONAL_GOVERNED_DIRECTORIES list (validation/repository/, tooling/) walked the same way as knowledge/ -- adding a future runbook location is now a one-line array edit, not a new bespoke code block. Second: markdown table rows were dropped outright rather than scanned, so an unquoted present-perfect sentence hiding in a table cell got no signal at all -- demonstrated by the reference's own §3 rule table, which already contains a present-perfect example ('The validator has read the file.') as an intentional 'Don't' illustration. Fixed by scanning table cells as discrete units (same forced-boundary treatment as list items) while stripping double-quoted spans from all prose first, so a cited or illustrative example in quotes -- exactly what the §3 table's Do/Don't columns are -- is read as data being discussed, not the document's own assertion. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this: the new runbook directory is scanned, an unquoted violation inside a table cell is caught, and the same violation stays exempt when quoted.

A fifth Codex review round caught three more real gaps, all fixed. First: run-audit.ts only echoed a passing step's full output under B2C_AUDIT_VERBOSE, a flag audit:ci never sets -- so the whole warning tier's 'real, non-blocking signal' promise was invisible in the one place CI actually reports results. Fixed at the shared orchestrator, not just this checker: every step's status line now carries a '(N warnings)' suffix parsed from the common reportAndExit summary, benefiting every two-tier validator repo-wide. Second: docs/platform/decisions-and-tradeoffs.md, an ADR as current and real as the two architecture docs already governed, was outside the hardcoded docs/ list. Added it explicitly, and left docs/platform/ as an explicit allowlist rather than a full directory scan on purpose -- documented inline -- since that directory also holds a historical audit, a founder-journey narrative, and an open backlog this repo's own conventions already keep outside every gate. Third, and most serious: the prior round's fix for table-cell quoted examples was a blanket double-quote strip applied to ALL prose, not just table cells -- so an ordinary quoted UI string or error message inside a real sentence lost its own violation along with its quote marks, anywhere in the governed surface, not only in tables. Replaced the blanket strip with a narrow, structural exemption: only a table cell whose entire trimmed content is a single quoted string is dropped; a partial or embedded quote, in a table cell or plain prose, stays fully counted. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: the ADR now gets scanned, a present-perfect phrase hidden inside a quoted UI string in plain prose is still caught, and a table cell with only a partial quote is still caught (while the whole-cell illustrative-example case from the prior round stays exempt).

A sixth Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: docs/implementation/graph-execution-v2.md -- the current guide for the graph compiler, durable runtime, scheduler, and verification boundary, named as such by docs/implementation/README.md -- was outside the hardcoded docs/ list. Added it. Second, and more serious: the sentence-splitting regex read every period as a candidate sentence boundary, including both periods inside an abbreviation like 'e.g.' and the periods inside a decimal or version number like 'v0.114.0' -- so a real, single grammatical sentence over the 20-word ceiling could pass by fragmenting into short-looking pieces at each of those periods, exactly as this repo's own knowledge/process/flow-traceability.md demonstrated live. Fixed by protecting a fixed set of common abbreviation periods (e.g., i.e., etc., vs., approx., cf., fig., mr./mrs./ms./dr./jr./sr., et al.) and any period directly between two digits with a Private-Use-Area sentinel character before sentence-splitting, then restoring it to a literal period once boundaries are final -- deliberately excluding ambiguous short words like 'no.' and 'st.' that are common as ordinary sentence-final words, where protecting the period would merge a real sentence boundary into the next sentence instead of fixing a false split. Caught and fixed a self-introduced regression from the first attempt at this same fix in the same review round: placing the new module-level consts after the file's already-running top-level scan loop threw a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError, and a stray leftover duplicate of the same block after the fix caused a duplicate-declaration build failure -- both fixed by consolidating the declarations once, in one place, above every call site. Four new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: the new architecture guide is scanned, a sentence that would otherwise fragment around 'e.g.' is still caught as one long sentence, and the same is proven for a version-number period.

A seventh Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: a list item's own marker ('-', '1.', '- [ ]') was left in the text before counting words, so it counted as a word itself -- a genuinely compliant 20-word bullet was reported as 21 and could fail an error-tier file. Fixed by stripping the marker, and any GFM task-list checkbox right after it, before the word count runs; the marker is still used to detect that a line is a list item, only the counted text changes. Second, and more serious: the prior round's abbreviation-period fix protected the period whenever ANY whitespace followed, even when that period was also the abbreviation's OWN sentence ending -- so two independent, individually compliant sentences ('Use the standard process, etc.' plus a fresh sentence right after) could merge into one over-long blob and produce a false violation, the opposite failure mode from the one that fix was written to close. Narrowed to only protect the period when a lowercase letter follows: that is what a genuine mid-sentence abbreviation looks like, while a sentence-final one is followed by a capital letter (the next sentence) or nothing at all. Caught and fixed a second self-introduced bug while verifying this same fix: the abbreviation-word regex needs its 'i' flag so 'E.g.' and 'e.g.' both match, but that same flag silently made a `[a-z]` lookahead on the same pattern match uppercase too, defeating the whole check -- moved the lowercase-continuation test out of the regex and into a case-sensitive plain-string check on the matched callback's own offset. Five new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: a compliant bullet and a compliant task-list bullet both pass, a genuinely over-length bullet is still caught after its marker is stripped, a sentence-final abbreviation stays a real boundary, and a mid-sentence abbreviation stays protected.

An eighth Codex review round caught three more real gaps, all fixed. First, and most serious: the previous round's lowercase-only check assumed a capitalized continuation always starts a new sentence, but this repo's own knowledge/engineering/backend-data-contract.md proved that wrong live -- 'a migration tool (e.g. Prisma Migrate, Alembic, node-pg-migrate) in the contract' has 'e.g.' followed by a capitalized product name mid-sentence, so the previous fix silently reintroduced round six's original false-split bug for the most common abbreviation in this repo's real prose. Fixed by splitting the abbreviation set in two: 'e.g.', 'i.e.', 'cf.', 'vs.', 'approx.', 'fig.', and 'et al.' grammatically always introduce more of the same sentence, so they are protected unconditionally regardless of what follows; only 'etc.' keeps the lowercase-only check from the previous round, since it is the one abbreviation in the set that commonly IS the last word of its own sentence. Second: '+' is a valid CommonMark unordered-list marker alongside '-' and '*', but the marker pattern only recognized the other two, so a compliant '+' bullet was not recognized as a list item at all -- its marker counted as an extra word, and it never got a forced sentence boundary. Added '+' to the marker pattern. Third: a list item that wraps onto a following physical line with no blank line between it is one logical sentence, but each physical line was getting its own forced boundary, so a real over-ceiling instruction could hide by fragmenting across its own soft wrap. Fixed by grouping a continuation line into its list item before the existing per-line processing runs, stopping at a blank line or any line that starts a new block. Six new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: e.g. before a capitalized product name still merges and gets caught, a compliant and a genuinely over-length '+' bullet both behave correctly, a wrapped list continuation is caught as one sentence, and grouping correctly stops at a blank line instead of merging an unrelated paragraph into the preceding bullet.

A ninth Codex review round caught three more real gaps, all fixed. First: platform/README.md documents provider configuration, execution API routes, environment variables, and deployment requirements -- a current API/config reference -- but was outside every discovery path. Added it to the governed allowlist. Second: the previous round's continuation grouping required a wrapped list-item line to be indented, but CommonMark's 'lazy continuation' rule also counts an UNindented follow-on line (no blank line before it) as part of the same list item, so an over-ceiling instruction could still hide by wrapping without indentation. Dropped the indentation requirement; the guard against merging unrelated content was never the indentation check anyway, it was requiring the previous grouped line to already be an active list item. Third, and most serious: the present-perfect heuristic recognized only five hard-coded intervening modifiers (not/never/already/just/recently), so 'The validator has successfully checked the file' -- present perfect, with an ordinary adverb the fixed list didn't cover -- passed undetected, even in the error-tier reference itself. Generalized to accept any \w+ly adverb (the regular English case) in addition to the fixed irregular words, zero or more repeated, between the auxiliary and the participle. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: platform/README.md is now scanned, an unindented wrapped list continuation is still caught as one sentence, and a present-perfect sentence with a general adverb is still caught.
